title: Join the Online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action’ on 7 December 2026
content:
Europa Nostra and the Office of Public Works Ireland (OPW) are hosting the online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action on Monday 7 December 2026 (13:00-14:30 CET / 12:00-13:30 WET).

This masterclass explores the methodology, practical experience and key outcomes of the initiative Improving the Energy Performance of Heritage Properties in State Care, which has been developed by OPW to support the country’s climate action commitments and the EU’s decarbonisation targets. At the time, no clear framework existed for improving the energy performance of historic buildings while safeguarding their heritage value. The initiative offers valuable insights and lessons learned that can be adapted and applied in other contexts and settings. The initiative received both a European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award and the Grand Prix 2026 in the Education, Training and Skills categories.

Register now

This online masterclass is organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, which is supported by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union.

title: Europa Nostra participates in the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters” held in Brussels
content:
Today, Europa Nostra is attending the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters – Debating and Communicating the MFF and National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs)”.

Building on yesterday’s Joint Statement by the Cultural Deal for Europe partners, which calls on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme, we must ensure that culture and heritage are also recognised across the EU’s other funding instruments, particularly the future National and Regional Partnership Plans for 2028–2034.

Photo credit: Europa Nostra

In her opening remarks, European Parliament President Roberta Metsola reminded us that the EU budget has a real impact on people’s lives. She stressed the importance of empowering cities and regions, involving local and regional authorities in designing and implementing the plans, and communicating what EU funding makes possible.

Why does heritage matter? Because the places, traditions and landscapes that shape our identity and sense of belonging also contribute to well-being, social cohesion, jobs, sustainable tourism and more attractive, resilient territories.

title: Joint Statement – Cultural Deal for Europe partners call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme
content:
The Cultural Deal for Europe is a trans-national, cross-sector partnership co-initiated by Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation

Ahead of the EU Economic and Financial Affairs Council of 10 November 2026, which will discuss the EU’s next budget (2028-2034), we, Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation – co-initiators of the Cultural Deal for Europe – call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to AgoraEU proposed by the Irish Presidency. Chopping €2.58 billion for culture, media, cultural heritage, and civil society – essential to Europe’s democratic resilience and hence the basis for our better future – would not only cause profound damage to an already heavily impacted culture (both arts and heritage) and media sectors but only save just 0.14% of the EU budget.

title: British-Turkish novelist Elif Shafak receives Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 in Lisbon
content:
“Literature has a very gentle but very profound power and resilience. It gives us hope and continues to connect us beyond all borders of identity, geography and time,” stated Elif Shafak, renowned British-Turkish novelist and storyteller after receiving the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 at a ceremony held on 5 November at the Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.

High-level representatives of the partners and supporters of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award – namely the President of Centro Nacional de Cultura, Maria Calado, the Secretary General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the representative of the Gulbenkian Foundation in the Award Jury, Guilherme d’Oliveira Martins – as well as the Mayor of Lisbon, Carlos Moedas, addressed the audience. The ceremony was attended by some 200 people. Among the guests of honour was the former President of Portugal, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa.

title: IN MEMORIAM: Dr. Andrea H. Schuler (1941–2026, Switzerland)
content:
It is with immense sadness that we bid farewell to Dr. Andrea H. Schuler 1941-2026), a highly committed Life Member and an esteemed former Executive President of Europa Nostra, who passed away on 2 November 2026. Europa Nostra expresses its gratitude for Dr. Andrea H. Schuler’s strong dedication to the cause of cultural heritage in Switzerland and in Europe as a whole.

Dr. Andrea H. Schuler at the headquarters of Europa Nostra in The Hague, 2008. Photo: Laurie Neale / Europa Nostra

Dr. Andrea H. Schuler was Vice-President of Domus Antiqua Helvetica – the Swiss Association of Owners of Historic Houses, Member of the Central Board of Schweizer Heimatschutz – the Swiss Heritage Society, and Member of the Board of a number of Swiss associations and foundations in the fields of heritage and music.

title: Potsdam to host new Europa Nostra Heritage Hub with a focus on climate resilience, civic engagement and youth capacity-building
content:
The State Capital City of Potsdam has entered into a strategic partnership with Europa Nostra, the leading European heritage civil society organisation. On 29 October 2026, a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Potsdam was signed at the Old Town Hall by Potsdam’s Lord Mayor Noosha Aubel, the Secretary-General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the President of Europa Nostra Germany, Dr. Uwe Koch. From 2027 onwards, the Hub in Potsdam will prioritise climate-resilient cultural heritage management, civic engagement and, above all, capacity-building for young people.

The new Hub brings together Potsdam’s local expertise and Europa Nostra’s transnational network. The Palaces and Parks of Potsdam, which are inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List, and the city itself serve as a real-world laboratory for the conservation of cultural landscapes in the context of climate change. To this end, close collaboration with local institutions, such as the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) and the Research Centre Sanssouci (RECS), is foreseen.

title: ANSCH Conference: Building bridges to protect cultural heritage amid conflict and climate challenges
content:
At the ANSCH (The Arab Network of Civil Society Organizations to Safeguard Cultural Heritage) Building Resilience Conference, supported by the Cultural Protection Fund of the British Council: “Building Resilience: Empowering Civil Society to Protect Heritage Amid Conflict and Climate Challenges,” held online on 19 October 2026, Europa Nostra Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović highlighted the vital role of civil society, local communities and international cooperation in safeguarding (endangered) cultural heritage.

Credit: Europa Nostra

During the panel “International Organisations and the Future of Heritage Protection,” she underscored four priorities: connecting organisations and networks, sharing knowledge and expertise, strengthening the voices of local civil society, and building lasting partnerships across the Mediterranean and beyond. She highlighted that Europa Nostra aspires to expand its work to benefit the entire area of “Mare Nostrum”.

Credit: Europa Nostra

title: Bánffy Castle in Răscruci, Romania, hosts ceremony to mark its European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award
content:
The official unveiling of the European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award 2026 plaque took place at Bánffy Castle in Răscruci, Cluj County, on 12 October, celebrating the exemplary restoration of this late 19th-century building. The ceremony brought together around 100 participants, including regional and local officials, heritage professionals and members of the community, to celebrate the collective effort behind the castle’s restoration.

An extensive rehabilitation project, valued at €11.5 million and funded primarily through European funds, has transformed the once-derelict estate into a vibrant cultural destination. The castle has rapidly become a major attraction in the region, welcoming nearly 20,000 visitors in the first nine months of 2026 alone and bringing renewed life to this important part of Transylvania’s heritage.

title: Europa Nostra expresses deep concern over the proposed cuts to the AgoraEU programme
content:
Europa Nostra stands in solidarity with the European cultural and civil society community and expresses its deep concern over the proposed cuts to the AgoraEU programme in the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU’s negotiating box for the EU’s 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), published on 10 October 2026.

The proposal would reduce the AgoraEU programme’s budget from the European Commission’s proposed €8.6 billion to €6 billion in current prices — a decrease of around 30%. With the next European Council Summit starting tomorrow, EU leaders have an opportunity to reconsider this proposal and maintain the level of ambition needed to support Europe’s cultural and democratic life.
